title: Short Stuff: Chameleons
summary: Short Stuff episode on chameleons. The hosts bust common myths: chameleons mainly change color to regulate body temperature and in response to emotion (excitement, agitation, fear), not to blend into surroundings, and their natural color is green-ish (yellow base with blue reflection when relaxed). They note chameleons cannot regrow their tails, unlike some lizards such as geckos. They compare chameleon color change to octopus chromatophores, explaining that chameleons use iridophores (crystal-like iridescent cells) that reflect light across the spectrum, controlled by hormones and muscles that expand or contract the cells, which is slower than the octopus's neuron-controlled sacks. Lizards seen in Georgia are discussed as likely skinks or leopard geckos rather than chameleons. The episode also includes a long digression about the movie Beetlejuice and Michael Keaton. Cliffhanger and ad break occur mid-episode.

segments.title: Opening banter and lizard misidentification
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the chameleon topic and discuss lizards seen in Georgia, debating whether they are skinks or leopard geckos, and mention skink toxicity.

segments.title: Chameleon tail and color change myths
segments.summary: Hosts note chameleons cannot regrow their tails, and bust the myth that chameleons change color to blend into surroundings; color change is tied to temperature regulation and emotion.

segments.title: Chromatophores versus iridophores
segments.summary: Hosts compare octopus chromatophore pigment sacks with chameleon iridophores, which are iridescent crystal-like cells that reflect light rather than use pigment.

segments.title: Ad break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break with a cliffhanger and a sponsor/ad segment.

segments.title: How chameleon cells produce colors
segments.summary: Relaxed iridophores reflect short-wavelength blue light, while excited cells spread apart to reflect red and orange; hormones trigger this, making chameleon color change slower than octopus neuron-controlled changes. Chameleons' natural color is yellow-based and appears green when relaxed.

segments.title: Beetlejuice and Michael Keaton digression
segments.summary: Hosts digress into their favorite Beetlejuice lines and songs, mention a possible sequel, and discuss Michael Keaton's early stand-up and a meeting with him.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts wrap up the chameleon topic and sign off the Short Stuff episode.
